items.problem: The validator's background-task check passes whenever a windows.backgroundTasks <Extension> exists, so it gave a green result on this in-process migration while the Run control was still dead. The existing MIGRATION-PATTERNS guidance about surfacing Register() failures is also written only for the out-of-process case.
items.evidence: Validate-UwpMigration.ps1:388-398 (PASS if manifest matches 'windows.backgroundTasks'); Package.appxmanifest:31-42 declares that extension; yet migration-score.json scenarios 3 & 4 = partial (dead Run). MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md:357 mentions try/catch + status only under the out-of-process model.
items.covered_at: Validate-UwpMigration.ps1 section 5c (lines 373-399) 'Retained manifest <Extension>s must be carried into the build manifest'; MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md > Background Tasks item 2 (line 357).
items.proposed_improvement: Extend the SAME validator branch so that when retained BackgroundTaskBuilder code has NO TaskEntryPoint assignment (in-process model), it FAILs/WARNs unless an OnBackgroundActivated handler exists, and prints the in-process pointer. Extend the PATTERNS 'surface the failure in the UI' note to apply to any BackgroundTaskBuilder registration (both models) and to warn that the UWP sample's HRESULT-specific catch is too narrow on WinUI 3.
items.generalizes: A validator that only checks extension presence will keep passing in-process migrations across scenarios; broadening the check and the always-surface-status rule prevents the silent dead-control regression class generally, not just for BLE.
